Subject: Request: per-1M IO rate baseline + model roster

Hi Diego,

Quick intro — I run the AI platform at Lumina Health. We’re evaluating hosted inference providers for a patient-facing summarization feature. Can you share your standard per-1M token IO pricing (input vs output split) for the hosted API and a current list of supported models (and guidance on latency tiers)?

A few helpful data points:
- Expected pilot: ~250k–1M tokens/month; production could grow to ~5–10M tokens/mo after 6–9 months.
- We care about output cost (summary length) and want to understand cost sensitivity with various models.
- We need EU region hosting and SOC2 / data residency info (we can request security docs later).

If you have a short one-pager or a rate sheet and a model catalog CSV, that’d be great — we’d like something we can share with finance.

Thanks —
Olivia

Hi Olivia — thanks for the note and the context. I’ve attached our Q3 hosted ratecard and a snapshot of the model catalog for EU-hosted options. High-level bullets below so you can skim quickly:

- Baseline hosted IO pricing (per 1M tokens):
  • Input tokens: $0.40 / 1M
  • Output tokens: $0.85 / 1M
  • Note: pricing above is for our standard family (r-infer-s). Lower-latency, larger models and low-precision quantized variants have different IO splits (see attached CSV).
- Typical model families included in the attachment: r-infer-s-7b, r-infer-m-13b, open-llama-70b-quant, community-compat-33b, and a responsibly-curated selection of instruction-tuned variants.
- Latency tiers: standard (50–150ms/token average), low-latency (20–60ms/token) for optimized families; we included measured medians per region in the ratecard.
- Discounts: we offer tiered volume discounts (5–20%) on hosted IO for 12mo commits and a 15% pilot credit for early pilots we approve.

Hi Olivia — quick answers inline and next steps below.

On Tue, Jun 26, 2028 at 08:11 AM Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@luminahealth.ai> wrote:
> 1) Token split: our average prompt is ~500 input tokens and summaries average ~120 output tokens — can you confirm how that maps to expected per-session cost?

Using the baseline rates I sent: 500 input tokens = 0.5 * $0.40 / 1M = $0.0000002? (see note below) — easier to think in per-1k tokens:
- Input: $0.40 / 1M → $0.00000040 per token → 500 tokens ≈ $0.00020 per request
- Output: $0.85 / 1M → $0.00000085 per token → 120 tokens ≈ $0.000102 per request
- Combined ≈ $0.00030 per summary request at baseline (before discounts).

(We generally model at 1M tokens = $0.40 for input and $0.85 for output; multiply by expected volume to estimate monthly cost.)

> 2) EU region: we need confirmation that the EU-hosted ratecard applies to data residency and that SOC2 / customer audit artifacts are available

Confirmed — the attached ratecard is for EU-hosted capacity and we can provide SOC 2 Type II report extracts and an IPAR/security pack under NDA. I’ll have our security team reach out via your procurement contact once you share the questionnaire.

> 3) Function-calling / structured outputs: good to know supported — does that carry any pricing surcharge?

No surcharge for function-calling. Pricing is token-based only. If you require guaranteed sub-50ms latency we recommend Dedicated capacity and that has a different commit/price model (happy to provide a Dedicated estimate if you’d like).

Pilot discount application: the 15% pilot credit is applied to gross IO spend for the pilot billing period (it is applied before any volume rebates).

Next steps:
- I’ve re-attached the ratecard and model CSV to this thread.
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/23456 (I’ll create a MAP and send a calendar invite for a technical walk-through).
- DocuSign MSA (optional early start): https://www.docusign.com/abc123-MSA

Let me know a couple of times that work for a 30-min walkthrough this week.

Best,
Diego
